subject.title: [Feature]:  Missing Session Management Commands in OpenClaw

question: What public session lifecycle contract should OpenClaw expose for stop, kill, pause, resume, and resource limits across Gateway, CLI, and UI?
rationale: Current main has partial abort/delete/cleanup/compact and admin subagent-kill primitives, but choosing the unified lifecycle semantics affects security boundaries, compatibility, child-process ownership, and user-facing UI behavior.

options.title: Design Additive Lifecycle Contract
options.body: Add explicit guarded Gateway methods and then map CLI/UI affordances to them while preserving current abort/delete defaults and documenting upgrade behavior.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Work
options.body: Keep this umbrella as coordination and route process kill, topic UI, resume/fork, and diagnostics to their narrower issues or PRs before adding broad APIs.

options.title: Defer Broad Controls
options.body: Keep current abort/delete/cleanup behavior and document the limitations until resource and process lifecycle ownership is designed.

recommendation.title: Design Additive Lifecycle Contract
recommendation.body: Add explicit guarded Gateway methods and then map CLI/UI affordances to them while preserving current abort/delete defaults and documenting upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history across the Gateway, CLI, and docs surfaces the product decision would touch.
